spec.reading: the E61 identity total = timing + selection read at every E219 rung: timing is derived by subtraction from the published total and selection, so it inherits the selection term's error and is not an independent burn
spec.movement_rule: a rung step is timing-carried when the timing part moves in the same direction as the total, and selection-resisted when the selection part moves against it
spec.invariance_rule: timing is width-invariant only if its rung-to-rung range fits inside the tightest control's standard error -- the same test E219 applied to the total

honest: timing is a subtraction, not a burn: with only the published total and selection in hand it inherits that selection term's own error, and a rung whose identity_ok is false is listed in identity_broken_widths rather than silently trusted
cost x0 throughout: neither arm carries a fee, so a movement of this size is gross of costs
where pool_binds is true the wide rung could not fill pick_n at every session, so that rung holds a narrower book than its label
the label reports which part CARRIES the movement; it does not claim the timing part is an exploitable effect, and a width-invariant timing part would still need a cost arm before any such reading
descriptive census only: no gate, no prereg, no trial count
